### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9a98a4675683a405aa911cd6c3e31f88bfe24151` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bc6aafdbc8f7ff0972552bb7c924149e0b5c6eef` — the merge of head `064e714dfb19a7caed674bab07df13922349bf53` into base `9a98a4675683a405aa911cd6c3e31f88bfe24151`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bc6aafdbc8f7ff0972552bb7c924149e0b5c6eef && git checkout bc6aafdbc8f7ff0972552bb7c924149e0b5c6eef
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9a98a4675683a405aa911cd6c3e31f88bfe24151 064e714dfb19a7caed674bab07df13922349bf53 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9a98a4675683a405aa911cd6c3e31f88bfe24151 && git merge --no-ff 064e714dfb19a7caed674bab07df13922349bf53

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9a98a4675683a405aa911cd6c3e31f88bfe24151
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9a98a4675683a405aa911cd6c3e31f88bfe24151` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `064e714dfb19a7caed674bab07df13922349bf53`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #35418 (body, triage comment, claim comment), PR #36030 (body, 23-file list, the net diff `origin/main...pr-36030` at this head), and the 74 check-runs on this head. All 74 concluded `success` or `skipped`. None is failing, pending or cancelled. That includes Check Changeset, Type Check UI, Test Core 1-10, Test UI 1-16, Lint UI, Lint & Repo Gates, Spec property liveness and the PR-body guards. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts. Nothing was re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`ApprovalServiceOptions.positionLabelSource` (public: `ApprovalServiceOptions` is exported from `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`'s index). Verdict: RIGHT.**
   - The field is optional (`positionLabelSource?`). It is a function from a position name to a promise of a string or `undefined`.
   - With no source, `notePositionLabels` skips the declared-label step. A position with no pack label is left out of the map, and `labelledPosition` keeps the clause's name, which is the behaviour on `main`.
   - Failure is safe. The `await` is in a `try` with an empty `catch`. A non-string or whitespace answer is ignored. The integration test "a failing source does not fail the read" pins this.
   - Widening only. Nothing is removed and no existing member changes its type.
2. **Plugin wiring (`approvals-plugin.ts`). Verdict: RIGHT.**
   - The source resolves `ctx.getService('metadata')` lazily on each call, like the i18n source. A throw on an empty slot answers `undefined`, and so does a service with no `get` function.
   - It calls `metadata.get('position', positionName)` and returns `item.label` only when that is a non-empty string.
   - A rejection from `metadata.get` itself is not caught in the wiring, but the service's `try` catches it.
   - `position` is not in `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_METADATA_TYPES`, so `MetadataManager.get` reads it by name. It cannot raise `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` here.
3. **Fallback order. Verdict: RIGHT where it applies.**
   - In `notePositionLabels`, the reader's pack comes first: `labels.positionLabel(name)`, which is `pick(positionLabelKey(name))`. `positionLabelKey` spells `positions.NAME.label`.
   - The pack is read in the locale that `negotiatedReaderLocale` returns. A miss echoes the key, and `render` treats that echo as `undefined`.
   - Second comes `positionLabelSource`, the declared `label`. Third, the map has no entry, so the internal name stands.
   - The key `positions.NAME.label` was already declared on `main` (`translation.zod.ts`, the `positions` face, which `translatePosition` overlays). The new key helper adds no new authorable key, and the existing round-trip test holds it to `TranslationDataSchema`.
   - The three-step order runs only when `readerLabels(context)` is defined, i.e. the read has a locale and an `i18n` service exists. See N1.
4. **The stored English audit comment. Verdict: RIGHT (unchanged).**
   - `ApprovalService.localizeRoutingNotes` builds `actions` freshly from `engine.find('sys_approval_action', …)` via `rowFromAction`. `overlay` assigns `row.comment` on that in-memory array only, and the method makes no write.
   - `adminRescueNoteText`'s no-`render` overload is the stored-English path. It never sees `positionLabel`, because the label map applies only inside the `render` branch.
   - The CONTROL test pins both the stored row (`'sales_manager'`) and the served text of a no-locale read.
   - `labelledPosition` rewrites only `approvalAdminRescuePositionUnheld` clauses. A `team:` literal with the same name keeps its name, which the unit test pins. `adminRescuePositions` de-duplicates names and drops empty or non-position slots.
5. **The `ReaderLabels.positionLabel` member, the third parameter of `adminRescueNoteText`, and the `PositionLabelOf`, `adminRescuePositions` and `positionLabelKey` exports. Verdict: RIGHT (internal).**
   - None of these is re-exported from the package index, and nothing outside `plugin-approvals` references `ReaderLabels`.
   - Adding a required member to that interface therefore narrows no published surface.
6. **Console (`ApprovalActionTimeline.tsx`, new `utils/approvalSystemNote.ts`). Verdict: RIGHT.**
   - `actorName`: `system:sla` is checked first and keeps "System (SLA)". After that, a falsy `actor_id` gives `approvalsInbox.systemActor` ("System"). Otherwise the label is `actor_name` or the `formatIdentity` output, as before.
   - `actor_name` is only ever set from a resolved `actor_id` (the server's `resolveUserNames` loop). So no person row without an `actor_id` loses its name.
   - `actionText`: `isSystemNote` (a `comment` row with no `actor_id`) is tested first and gives `approvalsInbox.actSystemNote` ("System note"). A person's comment keeps "Commented", which the live control in the same DOM pins. A no-actor `cancel` keeps its kind and names "System".
   - Both render surfaces use this one component: `RecordApprovalsPanel` and `ApprovalDecisionPanel`'s thread. `DecisionComment` renders only approve, reject and revise rows, so it is unaffected.
7. **New i18n keys (public: `@object-ui/i18n` locale objects). Verdict: RIGHT.**
   - `approvalsInbox.systemActor` and `approvalsInbox.actSystemNote` are present in all eleven packs: ar, de, en, es, fr, ja, ko, pt-BR, ru, zh-Hans and zh-Hant.
   - Each pack places them beside `systemSlaActor` and `actComment` in the `approvalsInbox` block, which is the prefix `tr()` reads. The text is translated in every pack, never left in English.
   - The additions are additive only.
8. **Docs (`content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`). Verdict: RIGHT.**
   - The page says the row stores the English with the name, the reader is served their language with the label (pack, else declared label), and the note shows as a system note by the system. This matches the code.
   - The drift check's other hit, `flows.mdx`, names `ApprovalService` only generically and states nothing this diff changes. The release pages it listed are release-owned and were correctly left alone.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset:** `.changeset/35418-approval-timeline-system-notes.md` bumps four packages, each as `patch`: `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n` and `@object-ui/console`.
- **Clause-② line:** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is line-initial in both the changeset body and the PR body. It names the optional `ApprovalServiceOptions.positionLabelSource` and the two new `@object-ui/i18n` keys, and says nothing is removed. This is RIGHT: the diff publishes exactly those two widenings, plus internal helpers that are not exported.
- **Metadata-protocol line:** `Metadata-protocol: none` is RIGHT. No spec file changes, and `positions.NAME.label` was already authorable on `main`. No new key, value or metadata type reaches a metadata author.
- **Level:** under AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist item 3), kind `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. So `patch` is RIGHT.
- **The console bump:** `@object-ui/console` has no file in the diff. Its bump is harmless because it sits in the changeset `fixed` group with the other packages, and Check Changeset is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Permission or visibility effect of reading position labels through the metadata service. Answered; no escalation.**
  - `ctx.getService('metadata')` is the raw `MetadataManager` (`packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`). Its `get(type, name, packageId?)` takes no caller context, so the read runs as the system.
  - The per-caller gate for `/meta` documents lives in the REST layer (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`). This server-side read bypasses it.
  - What reaches the reader is one string: the position's `label`. The wiring reads no grants, holders or description.
  - That label is for a position whose machine name the same note already shows, on `main`, to every caller who passes `listActions`' own request-visibility gate. So the reader learns a friendlier name for a fact they could already read, not a new fact.
  - Metadata reads are not organization-partitioned since ADR-0131 D6 (the `metaCallerOrganizationId` note), and `position` is not package-slotted. So no other organization's or package's item can be served.
  - No `/meta` gate is weakened, and the gate's per-caller verdicts are unchanged. Recorded here as instructed. Seat: confirm with the security lane only if a deployment treats position labels as confidential where machine names are not. No such posture exists on `main`.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5). No finding.** `notePositionLabels` makes one metadata lookup by name for each position in the note's own abandoned slate. That set is bounded and de-duplicated, it is answered from the in-memory registry first, and it is not a data query. No ids are materialised and no in-app join is made over data rows, so there is nothing SQL could push down.
- **The dev's stated reading of the kind label. Answered and accepted.**
  - The card asked for the type to read 「转交」, or 「系统」 instead, and gave 「转交 · 系统 · …」 as its acceptance example.
  - The PR uses 「系统说明」 ("System note") for all three no-actor notes: admin routing, submitter exclusion and no approver. Not every such note is a hand-off, and telling them apart on the client would need a new field on the actions contract.
  - The reading was declared in the claim comment and in the PR body, before the review. No ruling on the card objects to it. 「系统说明」 is within the card's 「系统」 option, and the sentence itself carries the hand-off meaning.
- **Card acceptance: "no `crm_sales_manager` on the page".** Met for the admin_rescue routing note the card observed: the label comes from the pack or the declaration. The integration test asserts that the zh-CN text does not contain the name.
- **Dev follow-up: the no-approver note still names the machine name.** Answered as out of scope. That note's `who` parameter is stored pre-composed, the card's observed case does not include it, and the PR lists it as a follow-up. See N2.
- **The card's "do not change the routing rules" boundary. Held.** The diff touches only display paths. `__resolvedFrom`, slate replacement and admin routing are untouched.
- **Open questions.** The claim and the PR carry no `open_questions` entry.

Graded findings (none is must-fix or should-fix):

- **N1 (nit).** The declared-label fallback is reached only inside `localizeRoutingNotes` after `readerLabels(context)` returns labels. A read with no locale, or on a deployment with no `i18n` service, serves the stored English with the machine name, even when the position declares a `label`.
  - This is consistent with the stored-English CONTROL test and with the docs page, so it breaches no contract.
  - A later change could label the no-locale English too, if the card's acceptance is read as covering such readers.
- **N2 (nit).** The no-approver note's follow-up has no filed issue number. File it as a card under #34571 before #35418 closes, so the remaining machine name on that note stays visible.
- **N3 (nit).** `notePositionLabels` awaits its lookups one at a time. It also runs before `overlay` has confirmed that the rescue row is in `actions`. Both costs are negligible, given a bounded slate and a registry-first read. There is no correctness effect.
